column2: explanation (shown by the (i) buttons; the nearest described parent explains anything not listed)

The official Vulkan conformance tests (Khronos CTS). Every Vulkan driver is supposed to pass them. Each test checks one small thing and reports Pass, Fail, Not supported (the driver does not offer that feature, which is fine) or Crash.
The core Vulkan API: creating devices, buffers, images and pipelines, copies and blits, clears, limits and error handling. Most of the basic driver plumbing is tested here.
A handful of quick sanity checks: create a device, a sampler and a shader, draw a triangle and run a compute shader. If these fail, little else will work.
Copying and scaling data between buffers and images (vkCmdCopy*, vkCmdBlitImage, resolves), in many formats and sizes.
Clearing images and attachments to colours, depth and stencil values.
Checks that the driver answers basic questions (versions, properties) consistently.
How shaders find their resources: descriptor sets, push descriptors, buffer device addresses and descriptor buffers. Translation layers like DXVK and VKD3D rely on this heavily.
Cutting geometry at the screen edges and at user clip/cull planes, and depth clamping.
Compute shaders: dispatches, shared memory, barriers and workgroup sizes.
Basic compute shader programs: sums, copies, barriers and shared variables. Quick and broad.
Skipping draws and dispatches depending on a value in GPU memory (VK_EXT_conditional_rendering).
Vector-times-matrix maths for machine-learning style shaders (VK_NV_cooperative_vector). Usually not supported on phones.
Graph pipelines for neural-network work (VK_ARM_data_graph). Usually not supported on phones.
Depth buffer formats and depth range handling.
Large, partly filled and dynamically indexed descriptor arrays ("bindless" resources, used by DXVK and VKD3D).
Using several GPUs as one device. Phones have one GPU, so most of these report Not supported.
Device-generated commands: the GPU writes its own draw and dispatch commands.
Drawing: indexed and indirect draws, instancing, base vertex/instance and simple render passes. Good basic coverage of the 3D pipeline.
Draw tests inside classic render passes.
Plain draws of triangles, strips and fans with different vertex counts.
The same draw tests using dynamic rendering instead of render pass objects.
Image memory layouts shared with the display system (DRM format modifiers).
Pipeline settings that are changed while recording commands instead of being baked into the pipeline.
Per-pixel operations: early depth tests, scissor, occlusion and sample masks.
Ordered access to the same pixel from several fragment shader invocations.
Reading barycentric (triangle position) values in fragment shaders.
Variable rate shading: shading a group of pixels at once to save GPU work.
Geometry shaders: emitting primitives, layered rendering and primitive IDs.
Shader language features: loops, functions, built-in variables, atomics, operators and precision. Mostly tests the shader compiler.
Shaders found by fuzzing that crashed or were miscompiled by real drivers. Good at finding shader compiler bugs.
Images: load/store from shaders, formats, sizes, mip levels, swizzles, compression and host copies.
Qualcomm image-processing instructions (VK_QCOM_image_processing).
Framebuffers created without images attached up front.
Not real tests: they write what the driver reports (properties, features, limits, formats, extensions) into the log. Useful to compare two drivers side by side.
Allocating, mapping and binding GPU memory, memory requirements and external memory.
The Vulkan memory model: when writes from one shader invocation become visible to others.
Mesh and task shaders, the modern replacement for the vertex/geometry stages.
Rendering several views (for example left and right eye) in one pass.

Graphics pipeline state in many combinations: blending, depth/stencil, vertex input, multisampling, push constants, specialization constants and pipeline libraries. The biggest group, over a million tests.
Pipeline tests using ordinary (monolithic) pipelines.
What happens after the GPU hits a fault or the device is lost.
Protected memory for DRM video. Usually not supported.
Queries: occlusion counts, timestamps, pipeline statistics and transform feedback queries.
Turning triangles, lines and points into pixels: coverage rules, line styles, multisampling, provoking vertex, depth bias.
Ray queries from shaders (hardware ray tracing). The Adreno 722 has no ray tracing, so these report Not supported.
Ray tracing pipelines. Not supported on the Adreno 722.
How shader threads come back together after branches.

Render passes and dynamic rendering: attachments, load/store operations, subpasses, resolves and MSAA. Important for tiled GPUs like Adreno, where the driver chooses between GMEM (tile memory) and sysmem rendering.
Render pass tests with the original render pass API.
The same with the newer render pass 2 API.
The same with dynamic rendering (no render pass objects).
Out-of-range reads and writes must be safe: no crashes and no leaked data.
Aborting shaders on purpose (VK_KHR_shader_abort).
Shader objects (VK_EXT_shader_object), an alternative to pipelines; repeats many pipeline tests.
Sparse binding and residency: textures and buffers that are only partly backed by memory.
Hand-written SPIR-V shaders: tests the shader compiler on single instructions and edge cases.
Shader storage buffers: data layouts and access from shaders.
Subgroup (wave) operations: ballot, shuffle and arithmetic across neighbouring shader threads.
Barriers, semaphores, fences, events and timeline semaphores (original API).
The same synchronization coverage with the newer synchronization2 API.
Tensor resources for machine learning (VK_ARM_tensors). Usually not supported.
Tessellation shaders: patch sizes, spacing, winding and primitive generation.
Texture sampling: filtering, mip levels, wrap modes, compressed formats and shadow compare.
Capturing vertex shader output into buffers (used by games and by DXVK for Direct3D stream output).
Uniform buffers: data layouts and access patterns.
Vulkan Video decode and encode. Turned off in this build.
Window system integration: swapchains and presenting to the screen. Not supported in DriverLab's off-screen test mode.
YCbCr (video) image formats and colour conversion in samplers.

OpenGL ES test programs from the freedreno project (Rob Clark), as used by the adreno-cmdstream-gather app, plus two by DriverLab. Each one draws or computes something with the phone's own OpenGL ES driver so its GPU commands can be recorded and compared. They run on the system driver only. Pass = the program finished without an error.
Advanced blend modes (multiply, screen, overlay and so on, KHR_blend_equation_advanced), with multisampling.
Large draws into textures to stress memory bandwidth.
Blending into offscreen framebuffers with several render targets and colour formats.
Prints what the OpenGL ES driver supports (version, extensions, configs).
A simple program that copies data through a shader (buffer and uniform setup).
Clears the screen with different colours, depth and stencil values.
Clears offscreen framebuffers of different sizes and formats.
Compiles and runs a compute shader to look at the shader compiler's output.
2D blitter (C2D) composite test. Needs Qualcomm's libC2D2.so, which current phones do not ship, so it fails right away (the same happens in the original app).
2D blitter (C2D) composite with blend modes. Needs libC2D2.so (missing on current phones).
Compute shaders with different workgroup sizes and IDs.
2D blitter (C2D) copy between formats. Needs libC2D2.so (missing on current phones).
Draws a rotating cube.
Draws a textured cube with different texture filters.
Samples cube map textures of different sizes and formats.
Draws with every primitive type (points, lines, line loops, strips, triangles, fans).
Draws whose parameters come from a GPU buffer (indirect draws).
Turns pipeline states on and off (blend, depth, polygon offset, culling) between draws.
The classic "gears" demo scene.
2D blitter (C2D) framebuffer test. Needs libC2D2.so (missing on current phones).
2D blitter (C2D) solid fills. Needs libC2D2.so (missing on current phones).
2D blitter (C2D) fills of partial areas. Needs libC2D2.so (missing on current phones).
Integer and float vertex attributes and texture formats.
A fragment shader that writes its own depth value.
Image load/store and image atomics from shaders.
Instanced drawing with per-instance attribute divisors.
Passing integer values from the vertex to the fragment shader.
Uploads 2D array textures in many sizes and formats; used to work out how the GPU lays textures out in memory.
Reads the driver's limits (maximum sizes, counts) and context options.
Low-resolution Z (LRZ), Adreno's early depth rejection, with different depth, stencil and blend settings.
Rendering into individual mip levels of a texture.
Sampling mipmapped textures with different level-of-detail limits.
Rendering into several colour targets at once (MRT), with masks and depth/stencil.
Multisampled rendering and resolves in different formats and sample counts.
2D blitter (C2D) with several surfaces. Needs libC2D2.so (missing on current phones).
Framebuffers with no attachments (only side effects such as queries).
Written for DriverLab: draws once into the two layers of a texture array with GL_OVR_multiview and checks that layer 0 is red and layer 1 blue.
Reads GPU performance counters through GL_AMD_performance_monitor.
A shader pattern from the piglit test suite that some drivers got wrong.
The working variant of the piglit-bad shader, for comparison.
Draws a quad without any vertex attributes (positions made in the shader).
Draws a flat-coloured quad.
Draws a flat quad into offscreen framebuffers of different formats.
Draws flat quads at several window sizes.
Draws a textured quad, including shadow-compare sampling.
Draws with 3D textures of different types and sizes.
Draws textured quads with many texture sizes and formats.
Occlusion and other queries.
2D blitter (C2D) command replay. Needs libC2D2.so (missing on current phones).
Rendering that forces the driver to restore and resolve tile (GMEM) contents between passes.
Per-sample shading and sample masks with multisampling.
Shaders of growing size, to see how the driver handles large programs.
Rendering into sRGB framebuffers.
Shader storage buffers of different sizes.
Stencil buffer tests and operations.
Triangle strips with colour interpolated across them.
Many textures in the vertex and fragment shaders, with border colours.
Render to a texture, then sample it, in different formats and sample counts.
Checks texture memory layout parameters.
Multisampled textures (texelFetch from MSAA textures).
Written for DriverLab: uploads a known pattern to 2D (every mip level), 2D array and 3D textures in nine formats and checks every texel. The original app's version only printed its usage text.
Transform feedback (capturing vertex shader output into buffers).
A triangle and a quad with different sample counts and depth/stencil buffers.
A single triangle with colours blended across it.
Rendering to and sampling from UBWC-compressed images (Adreno's bandwidth compression).
2D blitter (C2D) copies with UBWC compression. Needs libC2D2.so (missing on current phones).
Many values passed from the vertex to the fragment shader.
Vertex attributes of different sizes and types.
